title: Unit Rates with Fractions
seo_title: Grade 7 Unit Rates with Fractions Worksheets: Complex Fractions and Rate Word Problems
standard_text: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units. For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction 1/2/1/4 miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 unit rates with fractions worksheets: divide fractions to find unit rates, complex fractions, compare rates, best buys and real-world rate problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Unit rate = first amount ÷ second amount. With fractions, multiply by the reciprocal.
key_sub: 1/2 mile in 1/4 hour: 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 1/2 × 4 = 2 miles per hour.
body_html:
Unit rates with fractions

A unit rate tells how much for 1 unit, like miles per 1 hour. Divide the first amount by the second. When the amounts are fractions, you get a complex fraction, a fraction divided by a fraction. Divide by multiplying by the reciprocal.

RateDivideMultiply by the reciprocalUnit rate
1/2 mile in 1/4 hour1/2 ÷ 1/41/2 × 42 miles per hour
2/3 cup for 1/3 batch2/3 ÷ 1/32/3 × 32 cups per batch
3/4 mile in 1/2 hour3/4 ÷ 1/23/4 × 21 1/2 miles per hour
Example

Maya walks 12 mile in 14 hour. What is her speed?

Miles ÷ hours: 12 ÷ 14.

Multiply by the reciprocal: 12 × 4 = 2.

Answer: 2 miles per hour

Example

A painter covers 13 of a wall in 23 hour. How much per hour?

13 ÷ 23 = 13 × 32 = 12.

Answer: 12 of the wall per hour

Common mistakes

  • Dividing the wrong way: miles per hour is miles ÷ hours, not hours ÷ miles.
  • Multiplying the fractions: 12 ÷ 14 is 2, not 18.
  • Forgetting that a unit rate is for 1 unit: always divide by the second amount.

faq.a: A rate for one unit of the second amount, such as 60 miles per 1 hour or $3 per 1 pound.

faq.q: How do you find a unit rate with fractions?
faq.a: Divide the first amount by the second. To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 1/2 × 4 = 2.
A fraction with a fraction in the numerator, the denominator or both, like (1/2)/(1/4). It means 1/2 ÷ 1/4.

faq.q: How do I compare two rates?
faq.a: Find both unit rates and compare them. For prices, the lower price per unit is the better buy.

sets.title: Dividing fractions for a unit rate

items.q: A snail crawls 12 meter in 2 minutes. How many meters does it crawl per minute?
items.e: Unit rate = 12 ÷ 2 = 12 × 12 = 14 meters per minute. Not 4: that divides the minutes by the meters, the wrong way round.

items.q: A printer prints 6 pages in 12 minute. How many pages per minute?
items.e: Unit rate = 6 ÷ 12 = 6 × 2 = 12 pages per minute. Not 112: that divides the minutes by the pages, the wrong way round.

items.q: A runner goes 10 laps in 23 hour. How many laps per hour?
items.e: Unit rate = 10 ÷ 23 = 10 × 32 = 15 laps per hour. Not 115: that divides the hours by the laps, the wrong way round.

items.q: A plant grows 34 inch in 3 weeks. How many inches per week?
items.e: Unit rate = 34 ÷ 3 = 34 × 13 = 14 inches per week. Not 4: that divides the weeks by the inches, the wrong way round.

items.q: A machine fills 5 bottles in 14 minute. How many bottles per minute?
items.e: Unit rate = 5 ÷ 14 = 5 × 4 = 20 bottles per minute. Not 120: that divides the minutes by the bottles, the wrong way round.

items.q: A tap drips 25 liter in 4 hours. How many liters per hour?
items.e: Unit rate = 25 ÷ 4 = 25 × 14 = 110 liters per hour. Not 10: that divides the hours by the liters, the wrong way round.

items.q: Leo reads 12 pages in 34 hour. How many pages per hour?
items.e: Unit rate = 12 ÷ 34 = 12 × 43 = 16 pages per hour. Not 116: that divides the hours by the pages, the wrong way round.

items.q: A worker paints 910 of a fence in 3 hours. What fraction of the fence per hour?
items.e: Unit rate = 910 ÷ 3 = 910 × 13 = 310 of the fence per hour. Not 3 13: that divides the hours by the of the fence, the wrong way round.

items.q: A pump moves 8 gallons in 25 minute. How many gallons per minute?
items.e: Unit rate = 8 ÷ 25 = 8 × 52 = 20 gallons per minute. Not 120: that divides the minutes by the gallons, the wrong way round.

items.q: A recipe uses 56 cup of sugar for 5 muffins. How much sugar per muffin?
items.e: Unit rate = 56 ÷ 5 = 56 × 15 = 16 cups per muffin. Not 6: that divides the muffins by the cups, the wrong way round.

items.e: A unit rate tells how much for 1 unit: 60 miles per 1 hour, $3 per 1 pound.

items.q: To find miles per hour, which do you divide?
items.e: The rate is the first unit per the second unit: miles ÷ hours.

items.q: Which is the same as 12 ÷ 14?
c: 12 × 14
items.e: Dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal: ÷ 1/4 is × 4.

items.q: Find 12 ÷ 14.
items.e: Multiply by the reciprocal: 12 × 4 = 2. Not 18: that multiplies without flipping.

items.q: Find 23 ÷ 16.
items.e: Multiply by the reciprocal: 23 × 6 = 4. Not 19: that multiplies without flipping.

items.q: Find 34 ÷ 38.
items.e: Multiply by the reciprocal: 34 × 83 = 2. Not 932: that multiplies without flipping.

items.q: Find 13 ÷ 12.
items.e: Multiply by the reciprocal: 13 × 2 = 23. Not 16: that multiplies without flipping.

items.q: Find 56 ÷ 512.
items.e: Multiply by the reciprocal: 56 × 125 = 2. Not 2572: that multiplies without flipping.

items.q: Find 14 ÷ 23.
items.e: Multiply by the reciprocal: 14 × 32 = 38. Not 16: that multiplies without flipping.

items.q: Find 78 ÷ 14.
items.e: Multiply by the reciprocal: 78 × 4 = 3 12. Not 732: that multiplies without flipping.
